svg.title: Why a blocked sender's mail came through: four questions
svg.desc: Four questions in order. One: is it in Spam, Junk or Trash? Yes means the block worked, because Gmail's and Outlook's Block file the mail there and do not refuse it. Two: did it arrive before the block? Yes means move it yourself, because Gmail's Block and Outlook rules act on new mail. Three: is it from an address you did not block? Yes means an address block covers one address; block the domain after checking what it matches. Four: was the block made in one mail app? Yes means it holds on that device while the app runs; make it on the provider's server. If none applies, check in the provider's settings that the block is there and switched on.
svg.text: A blocked sender's mail came through
1. Is it in Spam, Junk or Trash?
Yes: the block worked. Gmail's and
Outlook's Block file it there, not refuse it.
No, it is in the inbox
2. Did it arrive before the block?
Yes: Gmail's Block and Outlook rules act
on new mail. Move this one yourself.
3. Is it from an address you did not block?
Yes: an address block covers one address.
Block the domain, after checking its match.
No, it is the same address
4. Was the block made in one mail app?
Yes: it holds on that device, while the app
runs. Make it on the provider's server.
None of these: check in the provider's settings
that the block is there and switched on.
